tier: Official — City & County of San Francisco
title: Learn about rent increases in San Francisco
supports: Current allowable increase 1.6% (3/1/2026–2/28/2027); once per 12 months; base rent only; no rounding up; 30/90-day notice; rent increase license; additional occupants cannot be charged; anniversary date rules.

tier: Official — City & County of San Francisco
publisher: SF Rent Board (sf.gov) news release, 14 Jan 2026
title: Annual Rent Increase for 3/1/26 – 2/28/27 Announced
supports: 1.6% effective 3/1/2026–2/28/2027; prior year 1.4% (3/1/2025–2/28/2026); worked dollar example.

tier: Official — City & County of San Francisco
title: Allowable Annual Rent Increases (full historical table)
supports: Every allowable annual increase percentage from 4/1/1982 through 2/28/2027.

tier: Official — City & County of San Francisco
title: Banked rent increases
supports: Banking since 4/1/1982; no cap on banked amount; not compounded or prorated; does not expire during a tenancy; new owners may use predecessors' banked amounts; does not carry to a new tenant; states a 24-month test (see F01).

tier: Official — City & County of San Francisco
title: Annual rent increase for multiple years
supports: Multi-year increases are added, not compounded; no petition required; no rounding up; 30/35-day notice; worked 8.2% example.

tier: Official — City & County of San Francisco
title: Learn about San Francisco rental laws
supports: Rent control + just cause for units built on or before 13 June 1979 that are not single-family dwellings; list of partial/full exemptions; Property Information Map for build date.

tier: Official — City & County of San Francisco
publisher: SF Rent Board Rules and Regulations, Part IV
title: Rules 4.10 (Notice) and 4.12 (Banking)
supports: Verbatim text of Rule 4.12(a)/(b): 12-month banking test, one increase per 12 months, no compounding/rounding, disclosure of banked portion and dates; Rule 4.10(b): non-conforming increase is null and void.

tier: Official — City & County of San Francisco
title: Administrative Code Chapter 37 (Rent Ordinance) as amended 24 Nov 2024
supports: §37.3(a)(1) annual increase ≤60% of CPI and ≤7%, license required; §37.3(a)(2) banking; §37.3(a)(8) above-allowable increases need a §37.8 petition; §37.3(a)(11) no increase for additional occupants; §37.3(b) notice content and void-if-nonconforming; §37.10C algorithmic-device ban.

tier: Official — City & County of San Francisco
title: The Rent Board Housing Inventory / rent increase license
supports: Annual reporting deadline 1 March; a rent increase license is required before any annual or banked increase can take effect; notice is not enforceable without a license on the effective date.

tier: Official — City & County of San Francisco
title: Landlord Petitions and Passthroughs
supports: The six increase types that require a petition (capital improvement, O&M, special circumstances/comparable rents, Prop I rent history, utility passthrough, Rule 1.21); no filing fee; petitions must precede the notice.

tier: Official — City & County of San Francisco
title: Operating and Maintenance Expense Petitions
supports: O&M petition allows up to 7% extra only if O&M expenses rose more than the annual allowable increase over two comparison years; must be filed before the notice; becomes part of base rent.

tier: Official — City & County of San Francisco
title: Special Circumstances Petitions Based on Rents for Comparable Units
supports: "The mere fact that a long-standing tenant is paying significantly less than market rent is not considered an extraordinary circumstance"; petition required; one-time only; precludes other increases.

tier: Official — City & County of San Francisco
title: Tenant Petitions
supports: Free tenant petitions include Unlawful Rent Increase / determination of lawful rent and Tenant Summary Petition for an invalid notice; the Rent Board does not adjudicate harassment, discrimination or retaliation.

tier: Official — State of California
title: Civil Code §1947.12 (Tenant Protection Act / AB 1482)
supports: Statewide cap = 5% + CPI change, max 10%; max two increments per 12 months; new-tenancy reset; §1947.12(d)(3) exempts units under a stricter local ordinance.

tier: Official — State of California
title: Civil Code §827 (notice of rent increase)
supports: 30 days' notice if the increase is 10% or less; 90 days if greater than 10%; service personally or by mail per Code of Civil Procedure §1013; longer period controls if another law requires it.

tier: Official — State of California
title: Civil Code §1954.52 (Costa-Hawkins)
supports: Owner may set initial and subsequent rates for units with a certificate of occupancy after 1 Feb 1995 or that are separately alienable — the exemptions relied on by newer condos/SFRs, not by this 1940 multi-unit building.

tier: Official — State of California
title: Civil Code §1954.53 (vacancy re-pricing)
supports: An owner may establish the initial rental rate for a new tenancy, except where the prior tenancy was terminated by the owner's notice or a §827 change in terms.

tier: Official — State of California
title: Civil Code §1942.5 (retaliation)
supports: A landlord may not increase rent or reduce services in retaliation for a tenant's repair complaint, agency complaint, inspection, or tenant-organising activity, including a 180-day window after specified tenant actions.

tier: Official — State of California
title: Government Code §12955 (FEHA — housing discrimination)
supports: Unlawful for an owner to discriminate or harass because of race, color, religion, sex, gender identity/expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran/military status or genetic information; §12955(f) bars retaliatory eviction/discrimination.

tier: Official — Federal
publisher: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development
title: Housing Discrimination Under the Fair Housing Act
supports: Federal Fair Housing Act prohibits discrimination in rental housing because of race, color, national origin, religion, sex, familial status or disability.

tier: Official — City & County of San Francisco
title: Rent Board Referral Listing (free and low-cost tenant resources)
supports: Official list of tenant legal/counselling resources, including Eviction Defense Collaborative, Bay Area Legal Aid, SF Tenants Union, Tenants Together, Advancing Justice–Asian Law Caucus, Housing Rights Committee, and Open Door Legal with a Sunset office in ZIP 94122.

tier: Program operator (non-government)
title: What is Tenant Right to Counsel — Prop F
supports: City-funded Tenant Right to Counsel programme: tenants who received an eviction notice or an unlawful detainer and do not live with the landlord have a right to a free attorney, full-scope representation. EDC is named as the intake point in the Rent Board's official §37.9(c) notice form.

tier: Primary filing — SEC
title: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended 31 Dec 2024 (filed with the SEC)
supports: Institutional-owner practice: leases of one year or less; staggering lease expirations to seasonal demand; premium pricing for customer segments; centralised renewal activity; explicit statement that rents and renewal increases are limited by fair housing laws and by state/local rent regulations.

tier: Official — City & County of San Francisco
title: Civil Rights Division — housing discrimination complaints
supports: The City body that investigates and mediates discrimination complaints in housing, employment and public accommodations — the local forum for a discrimination claim (the Rent Board does not hear these).
